does: Warms eggs or yolks gently by whisking a little hot liquid into them, so that they can then join the hot liquid in the pan without turning to specks. The word here is for eggs, not for chocolate.

intro.what: Egg tempering gradually warms beaten eggs with hot liquid before they join the pan.
intro.why: It teaches you to control a temperature change so a creamy mixture does not become speckled egg.

how: Whisk the eggs or yolks, usually with the sugar, in a bowl big enough to take the liquid.
Heat the milk or cream until it steams. It must not be boiling.
Pour a little of the hot liquid onto the eggs in a thin stream while whisking all the time.
Add a little more in the same way, until the bowl feels warm to the touch.
Tip the warmed mixture back into the pan and finish over gentle heat, stirring.

cues.text: The bowl is warm and not hot, and the mixture is smooth with no threads of cooked egg.
The mixture is glossy and thinner than it was.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring the hot liquid in all at once, which cooks the egg into specks.
mistakes.fix: Pour a thin stream while whisking hard.

mistakes.mistake: Tipping the eggs into liquid that is boiling.
mistakes.fix: Take the liquid off the heat first, and warm the eggs with a little of it.

quiz.question: What is the aim of tempering eggs?
choices: To warm them gradually while keeping the mixture smooth.
To cook them into separate firm pieces first.
To cool the hot liquid completely before mixing.
quiz.because: Small whisked additions spread warmth through the eggs without a sudden local shock.

quiz.question: How should the first hot liquid be added?
choices: In a thin stream while whisking continuously.
Only after pouring the eggs into boiling liquid.
quiz.because: A slow stream and whisking distribute heat instead of allowing hot liquid to set isolated egg.

quiz.question: Which appearance suits tempered eggs?
choices: Speckled with separate cooked egg pieces.
Firm curds surrounded by thin liquid.
Smooth and glossy without threads of set egg.
quiz.because: The eggs should join the liquid as a continuous mixture rather than setting into strands.

quiz.question: Eggs form specks after hot liquid is poured in at once. What should change next time?
choices: Add the liquid gradually while whisking.
Keep the eggs still so the specks settle.
quiz.because: Gradual addition avoids concentrated heat setting parts of the eggs before they mix.

comes_after.why: The eggs are whisked first, and the hot liquid is whisked in.
